title: The Whereabouts of the Embarrassing Charm
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Heiji, Kazuha, Ran, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention, consistent with the old case file. case_type: attempted murder (victim Kunisue survives, regains consciousness by the end). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Corrections vs. the old lower-fidelity file: (1) the old file omitted a victim node entirely per its stated convention for attempted-murder cases -- the new file adds Kunisue Teruaki as a `person` node since he is a named, central figure with extensive screen time, matching the broadened node-coverage bar. (2) The old file's `owns` edge ran from the culprit (s3/Kyuma) to the home-run baseball -- the transcript shows the opposite: Kunisue caught and owned the ball, and Kyuma stole it from him during the assault; the new file corrects this to `owns: Kunisue->ball` plus a separate `steals: Kyuma->ball` edge. (3) The old file's single clue (baseball terminology used to describe a claimed soccer game) is accurate and kept, but a second genuinely comparative clue was added: the asymmetric pocket bulge (victim's empty right jacket pocket vs. an overstuffed back pants pocket), which is what let Conan and Heiji deduce a spherical object had been stolen and stuffed elsewhere to hide the missing bulge. The charm/photo B-plot involving Kazuha and Heiji is left out of the graph (per the detective-cast omission convention) since it does not involve any non-cast character and is orthogonal to the assault case itself; it is only referenced in Kunisue's attrs for context.

clues.desc: Kyuma claimed to be a soccer fan who watched the soccer game, but used baseball vocabulary (visitor, fan, ground) instead of the soccer equivalents (away, supporter, pitch) -- proves he was actually at the baseball game.

Kunisue's right jacket pocket was empty while his back pants pocket was abnormally stuffed with wallet, phone, and cigarettes -- the mismatch shows someone deliberately over-packed the pocket to hide that a round object had been removed from it.

edges.detail: begged repeatedly for the ball at the stadium after the catch, was refused and mocked
